rows.text: Thick green sputum with a fall in FEV1
Greasy, foul-smelling stools
Weight loss with low albumin
HbA1c 7.4%

rationale.correct: Cystic fibrosis affects the lungs and both the exocrine and endocrine pancreas.

perOption.r1:c2: Pseudomonas infection inflames and plugs the airways.

questions.educationalObjective: Analyze the systems involved in cystic fibrosis.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The client's most important problem is {{b1}}. The treatment most likely to improve the FEV1 is {{b2}} with {{b3}}.

options.text: ineffective airway clearance from infected, thick secretions
hyperglycemia
diarrhea
anxiety
IV antibiotics active against Pseudomonas
oral amoxicillin
a cough suppressant
bed rest
intensive airway clearance several times a day
fluid restriction
a low-calorie diet
lying flat to rest

rationale.correct: Clearing infected mucus is the priority: antibiotics against Pseudomonas plus intensive airway clearance.

perOption.b1:a: Mucus plugging with infection drives the fall in lung function.
perOption.b1:b: Needs treatment but does not explain the FEV1.
perOption.b2:a: For example, an IV beta-lactam plus tobramycin.
perOption.b2:c: Coughing clears secretions in CF; suppressing it is harmful.
perOption.b3:a: Chest physiotherapy, an oscillating vest and mucus-thinning inhalers.

perOption.r1:c2: CF organisms such as Pseudomonas spread between clients with CF.
perOption.r3:c1: Cross-infection between CF clients is dangerous.
perOption.r3:c2: Cross-infection between CF clients is dangerous.

questions.educationalObjective: Generate infection-control measures for cystic fibrosis.

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: IV ceftazidime and tobramycin, airway clearance four times daily, dornase alfa, nutrition consult, endocrinology consult.

questions.stem: Review the day 4 data. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hold the next tobramycin dose and notify the provider and pharmacy
Report the ringing in the ears
Draw future troughs just before a dose and peaks 30 minutes after an infusion ends
Give pancreatic enzymes with every meal and snack
Give the tobramycin as scheduled and recheck in 3 days
Encourage the client to limit fluids to reduce coughing

rationale.correct: Aminoglycosides need trough and peak monitoring; a high trough, rising creatinine or tinnitus means holding the dose.

perOption.a: A high trough with a rising creatinine shows accumulation and kidney injury.
perOption.b: Tinnitus is an early sign of aminoglycoside ototoxicity.
perOption.c: Correct timing makes the levels meaningful.
perOption.d: Enzymes work only when taken with food.
perOption.f: Fluids thin secretions and protect the kidneys.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

perOption.s6: Thin liquids are the most easily aspirated.
perOption.s8: Coughing while eating is a sign of aspiration.
perOption.s10: A wet voice means fluid near the vocal cords.
perOption.s12: Aspirated material usually goes to the right lower lobe.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of aspiration.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: Aspirated material most often reaches the {{b1}} because {{b2}}. Fever and crackles 6 hours after the meal suggest {{b3}}.

options.text: right lower lobe
left upper lobe
right upper lobe
left lower lobe
the right main bronchus is wider and more vertical
the left lung is smaller
the stroke affected the right side
the client coughed
aspiration pneumonitis that may become pneumonia
a new stroke
heart failure
an allergic reaction to coffee

rationale.correct: The right lower lobe is the usual site; early fever and crackles after aspiration suggest pneumonitis.

perOption.b1:a: The usual site in an upright client.
perOption.b1:c: More likely when the client is lying flat.
perOption.b2:a: Gravity carries material down the right side.
perOption.b2:c: Anatomy, not the weak side, decides this.
perOption.b3:a: Early chemical injury; bacterial infection may follow.

questions.stem: For each intervention, indicate whether it is indicated or contraindicated.

rows.text: Keep NPO until the swallow screen and speech therapy assessment
Head of the bed at 30 to 45 degrees at all times
Oral care with a toothbrush at least twice daily
Give oral medications crushed in applesauce until the screen is done
Oxygen to keep SpO2 at 92% or higher
Antibiotics covering oral flora if pneumonia develops, as prescribed

rationale.correct: Stop oral intake, position upright, clean the mouth, give oxygen, and treat infection if it develops.

perOption.r3:c1: Reduces oral bacteria that cause pneumonia.
perOption.r3:c2: Reduces oral bacteria that cause pneumonia.

questions.educationalObjective: Analyze antiviral use in an influenza outbreak.

questions.stem: Which resident should the charge nurse assess first?

options.text: Resident A, with SpO2 88%, respirations 28/min and new confusion
Resident B, with a temperature of 38.2 C (100.8 F) and diabetes that may be destabilized
Resident C, whose antiviral dose needs adjusting for kidney disease today
A UAP who reports a sore throat and wants to know whether to finish the shift

rationale.correct: The resident with hypoxemia, tachypnea and new confusion is the most unstable.

perOption.a: Signs of hypoxemic respiratory failure and delirium need assessment and likely transfer.
perOption.b: Needs glucose checks, but is stable.
perOption.c: Important, but not the most urgent.
perOption.d: Handled promptly by sending the UAP home, but the hypoxemic resident comes first.

questions.stem: For each area of the outbreak plan, select the measures the charge nurse should put in place.

options.text: Droplet precautions for residents with symptoms
Keep ill residents in their rooms, or cohort them together
Hold the weekly group bingo as usual to keep spirits up
Staff with fever or symptoms stay home until 24 hours fever-free without medicine
Offer vaccination to unvaccinated staff
Have the same staff care for ill and well residents on one shift
Post signs and screen visitors for symptoms
Encourage visitors to take residents to the dining room

rationale.correct: Droplet precautions, cohorting, pausing group activities, excluding ill staff and screening visitors control an outbreak.

exhibits.body: The infection preventionist confirms an outbreak and asks the charge nurse to start the facility outbreak plan.

questions.stem: Review the medication orders. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Clarify Resident C's dose with the provider before giving it
Give Resident A's first dose now
Watch for new confusion or unusual behavior after starting oseltamivir

rationale.correct: Start antivirals promptly, adjust doses for kidney function and watch for adverse effects.

perOption.a: With creatinine clearance of 25 mL/min, the treatment dose is reduced, about 30 mg once daily.
perOption.b: Antivirals still help in severe illness after 48 hours.
perOption.c: Neuropsychiatric effects are reported, though rare.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The priority is to relieve {{b1}} with {{b2}}. Because the effusion is likely to recur, the team should also discuss {{b3}}.

options.text: dyspnea from lung compression
pain
infection
anxiety alone
therapeutic thoracentesis
a diuretic
bronchodilators
chest physiotherapy
goals of care and options such as an indwelling pleural catheter
repeat thoracentesis every few days in hospital

perOption.b1:a: The effusion compresses the lung and causes hypoxemia.
perOption.b1:d: The dyspnea has a physical cause.
perOption.b2:a: Draining the fluid quickly re-expands the lung.
perOption.b2:b: Malignant effusions do not respond to diuretics.

perOption.b3:b: Contrary to the client's stated wish.

questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse plan for the thoracentesis? Select all that apply.

options.text: Confirm that informed consent is signed
Sit the client upright, leaning forward over a bedside table
Tell the client not to cough, talk or move during needle insertion
Monitor SpO2, breathing and blood pressure throughout
Check that the platelet count and INR are in a safe range
Position the client flat on the back with arms at the sides
Keep the client NPO for 12 hours before

rationale.correct: Thoracentesis needs consent, an upright leaning position, stillness during insertion and close monitoring.

perOption.b: Spreads the ribs and pools fluid at the base.
perOption.e: Lowers the risk of bleeding from the needle.
perOption.f: Fluid would not pool for safe access.

exhibits.body: SpO2 95% on room air after drainage of 1,300 mL. The client is comfortable and asks about going home.

exhibits.title: Pulmonary unit, admission
exhibits.body: A 22-year-old client with cystic fibrosis is admitted with 2 weeks of more sputum, now thick and green, worse cough, fatigue and a 3 kg weight loss. FEV1 is 48% of predicted (65% three months ago). Sputum has grown Pseudomonas aeruginosa before. The client reports greasy, foul-smelling stools and has been "skipping the enzyme capsules when eating on the go." Another client with cystic fibrosis is in a room on the same unit.

exhibits.title: Stroke unit, day 2
exhibits.body: A 76-year-old client had a left hemisphere ischemic stroke 2 days ago, with right-sided weakness and slurred speech. The bedside swallow screen has not been done yet; the chart says NPO. At 0800 a UAP fed the client breakfast with thin coffee, saying the client "looked hungry." The client coughed during the meal and the voice sounded wet afterward. At 1400 the client is breathless.

exhibits.title: Long-term care unit, Tuesday 0700
exhibits.body: The RN is the charge nurse on a 30-bed long-term care unit. Since Sunday, three residents have developed fever, cough and muscle aches. Rapid influenza A tests are positive for all three. About 60% of staff are vaccinated this season.

cells: Temperature 38.9 C (102 F), RR 28/min, SpO2 88%, new confusion; symptoms began Sunday

rows.label: Resident B, 79 years, diabetes
cells: Temperature 38.2 C (100.8 F), RR 20/min, SpO2 95%, eating; symptoms began Monday

rows.label: Resident C, 91 years, kidney disease (creatinine clearance 25 mL/min)

caseStudies.title: Malignant pleural effusion and goals of care

exhibits.title: Oncology unit
exhibits.body: A 68-year-old client with metastatic lung cancer has had worsening shortness of breath for a week and now cannot lie flat. Breath sounds are absent over the lower two-thirds of the left chest, with dullness to percussion and reduced tactile fremitus. The trachea is shifted slightly to the right. testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
